corpus.source: [2026.07.27]-lore-test-inbox-500-v1 (1).html (The Ellington Mailbox, synthetic CT town-clerk inbox)
corpus.note: classes are litigation/FOIA-response ROLES, not topics; scored as separability

harness.path: classify_untagged (core/lore/classify.py), fresh sqlite DB, emails as notes (headers+body, updated_at=email date, newest-first)
harness.truncation_exposure: median body 321 chars; 1/494 emails lose >50% of body to the 500-char window

pairwise_vs_thread.note: P meaningless (30 topics vs 280 tiny threads); R=0.866 = same-conversation emails stay in one topic

class_recovery.Exhibit 1: Somers Road Solar 57/71 + Solar Development 11 (semantic split; slug registry cannot merge — topic_merge.py territory)
class_recovery.Exhibit 2: same solar topics as Ex1 (expected: 20 dual-labeled) + Records Management 9
class_recovery.Exhibit 3: Vital Records 7 + Genealogy Records 5 (2 topics cover 12/12)
class_recovery.Personal: 12 clean personal-life topics (Personal Events, Cottage Rental, Utility Bills...)
class_recovery.Context: 15 municipal-business topics (Land Records, Records Management, Vital Records, Elections...)

spam.miss_pattern: gray bulk mail — CCM weekly digests, IIMC/NEMCI training + certification blasts, grant alerts, conference registration, insurance quotes — filed by subject matter into work topics

verdict: Topic-level tagging is sound: 30 coherent topics (no cold-start fragmentation), matters recoverable in 1-3 topics each, conversations stay together (thread-pair R 0.866). The architecture has NO role axis: unsolicited/bulk mail that mimics domain vocabulary lands in real work topics ~50% of the time. Fix candidates: (a) prompt line steering solicitation to a reserved Spam topic, (b) role field in the JSON contract, (c) filter at recall time.
